title: Migrate Claude from plugin distribution to a CLI-managed adapter
objective: Claude users should receive the same CLI-owned Kyro runtime, skill routing, updates, and diagnostics as other hosts. Removing the separately installed Claude plugin eliminates a second release channel and stale plugin caches, while a documented, non-destructive migration prevents existing users from losing access or seeing duplicate commands.

tasks.title: Implement a safe CLI-managed Claude adapter
tasks.description: Make Claude installable through the existing adapter registry, projecting all seven router-first command skills into the native Claude skills root and integrating install, sync, doctor, and uninstall ownership.
tasks.context: Reuse the shared command-skill projection and existing operation-plan safeguards. Preserve unrelated Claude files and never remove an external plugin. Test fresh installation, idempotence, collisions, stale projection diagnostics, and coexistence with other adapters.
acceptanceCriteria: Claude is an implemented adapter and `kyro install --agent claude` projects exactly the seven public Kyro command skills through the shared runtime.
Install, sync, doctor, and uninstall preserve unrelated Claude content, detect missing or stale managed skills, and fail closed on unsafe or foreign paths.
Disposable fixtures prove repeat installation, coexistence with standard/Codex/OpenCode, and no automatic legacy-plugin removal.

evidence.summary: Implemented the CLI-managed Claude adapter with native router skills, guarded projection writes, migration warning, doctor checks, drift ownership, and disposable install/sync/uninstall regressions.

validations.note: TypeScript compiled and the workspace CLI was refreshed.
Disposable adapter fixtures covered collisions, symlinks, repair, repeat sync, coexistence preview, and legacy-plugin preservation.

evidence.notes: This is maker-reported task evidence. A real Claude UI discovery smoke remains a separate release gate.

tasks.title: Retire Claude plugin packaging and plugin-only fallbacks
tasks.description: Remove plugin manifests, wrappers, hooks, and their active package entries; replace plugin-specific doctor, version, startup, bundle, and packaging assumptions with adapter-focused checks.
tasks.context: Do not remove historical plans or changelog facts. Preserve portable CLI guard checks and root runtime assets. The tarball must not contain retired plugin assets, and the active instructions must not invoke CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
acceptanceCriteria: The npm package excludes `.claude-plugin`, `providers/claude/commands`, and `hooks`, with automated absence assertions.
Doctor, version, startup, and bundle checks pass without plugin metadata or plugin-only CLI fallbacks.
The retired Claude-only Bash hooks are not represented as portable CLI enforcement, and existing Forge/Work CLI guard checks remain green.

evidence.summary: Retired Claude plugin manifests, wrappers, and host-only hooks from the package; removed plugin CLI fallbacks and converted version, doctor, startup, and bundle checks to the CLI-managed adapter contract.

tasks.title: Document Claude adapter installation and safe plugin migration

tasks.context: Keep historical release records intact. Explain that Kyro will not disable or uninstall a user's legacy plugin, and that real Claude UI discovery is a later release smoke gate rather than a claim proved by repository fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: Current documentation identifies `kyro install --agent claude` and `kyro update` as the Claude installation and update path and maps former plugin commands to native Kyro skills.
Migration guidance is non-destructive, names possible duplicate commands, and explains user-controlled removal of the old plugin.
Current safety documentation distinguishes CLI-owned guardrails from the removed Claude-only hooks, and documentation links pass.

tasks.title: Verify plugin-free Claude integration and portable workflow parity
tasks.description: Run targeted and aggregate checks, isolated package/adapter smoke, artifact diagnostics, and source/package scans; fix regressions found before recording the final Work review.
tasks.context: Use the workspace build and disposable homes; do not install globally, release, commit, or push. Treat a real Claude host UI smoke as an explicit later release gate. Distinguish environmental doctor skew from implementation failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Build, targeted adapter and package checks, full `npm run check`, artifact doctor, analyze, package dry run, and `git diff --check` pass or any failure is reported without a pass claim.
Disposable package and adapter probes prove a plugin-free tarball, seven Claude skills, safe repeated installation/removal, and unchanged Forge/Work behavior.
The final evidence names verification limits and confirms no version bump, release, global installation, commit, or push occurred.
